ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: On a line, seven squares are placed in sequence (as shown). It is known that the areas of the three diagonally placed squares are 1, 2, and 3, respectively, and the areas of the four upright squares are $S_1$, $S_2$, $S_3$, and $S_4$. What is the value of $S_3 + S_4 - S_1 - S_2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Observe that, \\
$\because AB=BE$, and $\angle ACB=\angle BDE=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle ABC+\angle BAC=90^\circ$, and $\angle ABC+\angle EBD=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BAC=\angle EBD$, \\
$\because$ in triangles $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle BDE$, \\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle ACB=\angle BDE=90^\circ \\
\angle BAC=\angle EBD \\
AB=BE
\end{array}\right.$, \\
$\therefore \triangle ABC\cong \triangle BDE(\text{AAS})$, \\
$\therefore BC=ED$, \\
$\because AB^2=AC^2+BC^2$, \\
$\therefore AB^2=AC^2+ED^2={S}_{1}+{S}_{2}$, \\
i.e., ${S}_{1}+{S}_{2}=1$, \\
Similarly, ${S}_{3}+{S}_{4}=3$. \\
Hence, ${S}_{3}+{S}_{4}-{S}_{1}-{S}_{2}={S}_{3}+{S}_{4}-({S}_{1}+{S}_{2})=3-1=\boxed{2}$.

The adjacent two sides of this tilted square are equal and perpendicular to each other, so the two small right triangles formed by its left contact point, bottom vertex, right contact point and the baseline/vertical lines are congruent after rotation. Therefore S3+S4-S1-S2=(S3+S4)-(S1+S2)=3-1=2.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the seven squares alternate along one horizontal baseline as upright square S1, tilted square of area 1, upright square S2, tilted square of area 2, upright square S3, tilted square of area 3, upright square S4. For the tilted square of area 1, label its left contact point with S1, its bottom vertex on the baseline, and its right contact point with S2. Let the side lengths of S1 and S2 be a and b, so their areas are a^2=S1 and b^2=S2. The two small right triangles formed under the two adjacent sides of the tilted square are congruent/rotated because adjacent sides of a square are equal and perpendicular. Therefore the horizontal leg paired with one vertical height equals the other upright side length. Applying the Pythagorean theorem to one side of the tilted square gives its side squared as a^2+b^2, so S1+S2=1. Repeat the same local argument for the tilted square of area 3 between S3 and S4 to get S3+S4=3. Then compute (S3+S4)-(S1+S2)=3-1=2.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: along the horizontal line, each tilted square has its lower vertex on the baseline and its left and right vertices attached to the top inner corners of the neighboring upright squares. Prove a general coordinate lemma for any tilted square between upright squares of side lengths x and y. Put the lower vertex of the tilted square at the origin. Its left upper vertex has height x above the baseline, and its right upper vertex has height y above the baseline. If the vector from the lower vertex to the left vertex is (-p,x), then because the two sides of the tilted square meeting at the lower vertex are perpendicular and equal, the vector to the right vertex is the 90-degree rotation (x,p). Hence y=p. Therefore the tilted square side length squared is p^2+x^2=y^2+x^2, so its area equals x^2+y^2, the sum of the adjacent upright square areas. Apply this lemma to the first tilted square: S1+S2=1. Apply it to the third tilted square: S3+S4=3. Subtract to obtain S3+S4-S1-S2=2.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中在同一条水平基线上依次放置了七个正方形：第1、3、5、7个是直立正方形，面积分别标为 S1、S2、S3、S4；第2、4、6个是倾斜正方形，内部面积分别标为 1、2、3。每个倾斜正方形的下顶点落在水平基线上，它的左、右两个侧顶点分别连接到相邻两个直立正方形靠内侧的上顶点。

推理：证明一个通用引理。考虑任意一个夹在两个直立正方形之间的倾斜正方形。设左侧直立正方形边长为 x，右侧直立正方形边长为 y，因此它们面积分别为 x^2 和 y^2。把倾斜正方形的下顶点放在坐标原点。它左侧顶点的高度等于左侧直立正方形边长 x，故可设从下顶点到左侧顶点的向量为 (-p, x)。因为这是正方形，两条从下顶点出发的边等长且垂直，所以到右侧顶点的向量是 (-p, x) 的一个 90 度旋转，即 (x, p)。右侧顶点的高度等于右侧直立正方形边长 y，所以 y = p。于是该倾斜正方形的边长平方为 p^2 + x^2 = y^2 + x^2，也就是该倾斜正方形面积等于左右相邻两个直立正方形面积之和。

应用到第一个倾斜正方形：它的面积为 1，左右相邻直立正方形面积为 S1、S2，所以 S1 + S2 = 1。

raw_record.original_question: On a line, seven squares are placed in sequence (as shown). It is known that the areas of the three diagonally placed squares are 1, 2, and 3, respectively, and the areas of the four upright squares are $S_1$, $S_2$, $S_3$, and $S_4$. What is the value of $S_3 + S_4 - S_1 - S_2$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Observe that, \\
$\because AB=BE$, and $\angle ACB=\angle BDE=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle ABC+\angle BAC=90^\circ$, and $\angle ABC+\angle EBD=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BAC=\angle EBD$, \\
$\because$ in triangles $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle BDE$, \\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle ACB=\angle BDE=90^\circ \\
\angle BAC=\angle EBD \\
AB=BE
\end{array}\right.$, \\
$\therefore \triangle ABC\cong \triangle BDE(\text{AAS})$, \\
$\therefore BC=ED$, \\
$\because AB^2=AC^2+BC^2$, \\
$\therefore AB^2=AC^2+ED^2={S}_{1}+{S}_{2}$, \\
i.e., ${S}_{1}+{S}_{2}=1$, \\
Similarly, ${S}_{3}+{S}_{4}=3$. \\
Hence, ${S}_{3}+{S}_{4}-{S}_{1}-{S}_{2}={S}_{3}+{S}_{4}-({S}_{1}+{S}_{2})=3-1=\boxed{2}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the attached figure there is a horizontal baseline, and seven squares are placed in sequence on this line: the leftmost is an upright square S1, followed by a tilted square, with area 1 marked inside; next is an upright square S2; then a tilted square, with area 2 marked inside; next is an upright square S3; then a tilted square, with area 3 marked inside; the rightmost is an upright square S4. Below each tilted square there is a vertex lying on the baseline, and its left and right adjacent vertices respectively touch the upper corners of the upright squares on the two sides.
Reasoning: First look at the tilted square with area 1; it is sandwiched between the upright squares S1 and S2. Let the side lengths of S1 and S2 be a and b respectively, then S1=a^2, S2=b^2. The adjacent two sides of this tilted square are equal and perpendicular to each other, so the two small right triangles formed by its left contact point, bottom vertex, right contact point and the baseline/vertical lines are congruent after rotation. Therefore, the horizontal segment paired with the vertical height a on the left side is equal to b. Thus one side length L of the tilted square with area 1 satisfies L^2=a^2+b^2=S1+S2. Because the area of this tilted square is 1, S1+S2=1.
Similarly, for the tilted square with area 3, it is sandwiched between the upright squares S3 and S4, obtaining S3+S4=3.
Therefore S3+S4-S1-S2=(S3+S4)-(S1+S2)=3-1=2.
